skill.name: socialdatax-media-save-organizer
skill.description: Use SocialDataX to save supported social media images, video, or audio to a directory you choose. Track source links, local paths, and download results.
skill.summary: Save media from supported social links and record where each file came from.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts reflect Markdown formatting, ordinary Chinese prose, or configuration references. The workflow directs agents and users to run an unpinned CLI that can access credentials, and it leaves input handling and link redaction unspecified. No evidence of prompt injection or intentional credential exfiltration was found in the reviewed source.

remediation.issue: Authentication and media commands run a mutable npm release with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace all latest invocations with a reviewed, integrity-verified release. Require explicit approval before first installation or execution, and run it with limited privileges.

remediation.issue: The CLI can access a persistent credential and inherit environment secrets, even for operations that do not require authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Use platform-managed secrets or an OS credential store. Pass only the SocialDataX credential to authenticated operations and isolate direct downloads from credential files and environment secrets.

remediation.issue: Shell examples do not enforce separation between command syntax and untrusted input.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke the reviewed executable with separate arguments and no shell interpolation. Restrict writes to the approved output directory.

remediation.issue: The direct-download workflow does not specify how to restrict outbound destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Require approved public HTTPS media hosts. Verify destinations after DNS resolution and on each redirect, and deny access to private or local addresses.

remediation.issue: Reports may reproduce temporary access tokens from source or media links.
remediation.suggestion: Redact tokens and signatures from chat, logs, and manifests. Prefer stable public source links or content IDs in reports.

content.user_title: Save and Organize Social Media Files
content.value_statement: It is easy to lose track of which posts supplied downloaded media. Save files from supported links and record each source, local path, and outcome.
actual_capabilities: Resolve links from supported social platforms through SocialDataX detail lookups.
Save available images, video, or audio from supported media links into a chosen local directory.
Use the CLI to save Bilibili videos and merge audio and video when needed.
Download each distinct media URL once while recording all of its source posts.
Verify saved files and report source links, local paths, existing files, and failures.
limitations: Supports Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X, and Bilibili, not arbitrary websites.
Online lookups require configured SocialDataX authentication and may use account credits.
The CLI requires Node.js and npm. Merging Bilibili streams requires ffmpeg.
Bilibili support is for video links, not articles or feed posts. Its MCP tool returns links but does not save files.

use_cases.title: Archive campaign media
use_cases.description: Save selected campaign assets and record which post supplied each file.

use_cases.title: Collect media for a production
use_cases.description: Save approved clips and images to a project directory, and list any assets that could not be downloaded.

use_cases.title: Maintain a research archive
use_cases.description: Track media from multiple posts, keep all source references, and avoid downloading the same URL twice.

prompt_templates.title: Save one image
prompt_templates.scenario: A supported direct media link is already available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved SocialDataX CLI to save this image from [direct link] to [folder]. Confirm the file exists and report its path.

prompt_templates.title: Save media from one post
prompt_templates.scenario: A supported post link needs an online lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved SocialDataX setup to check [post link]. Save only its video to [folder] and report the source and verified path.

prompt_templates.title: Organize a batch of assets
prompt_templates.scenario: A list contains posts that may point to the same media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Process only [link list] with my approved setup. Save each distinct media URL once under [folder]. List every source and any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an existing archive
prompt_templates.scenario: An earlier batch has a source list and a mix of completed and failed downloads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [link list] with [existing source list] before downloading. Use my approved setup for missing media only. Update the list in [folder] and redact access tokens.

output_examples.input: Save the video from a supplied Douyin post to Campaign Media using the approved setup.
output_examples.output: Saved and verified one video from the supplied Douyin post at Campaign Media/material-001/clip.mp4.

output_examples.input: Resume a batch containing two Weibo posts that share one image and one unavailable X clip.
output: The shared Weibo image was already present and matched the source list. Both posts remain listed as sources.
The X clip could not be downloaded because its media link had expired. No file path was recorded.

best_practices: Use a reviewed, pinned SocialDataX CLI and approve any new installation explicitly.
Provide only links you are allowed to archive, and choose a dedicated local output directory.
Verify files before marking them saved, and remove access tokens from shared reports.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat, command arguments, logs, or source lists.
Do not pass a post page to a command that expects a direct media link.
Do not treat a skipped or failed download as a newly saved file.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X, and Bilibili video links.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX API key?
faq.answer: Supported direct media downloads do not require a key. Online post lookups and Bilibili video link retrieval need an authenticated setup.

faq.question: What do I need to run the CLI?
faq.answer: Use a reviewed, pinned SocialDataX release with Node.js and npm. Install ffmpeg if you need to merge Bilibili streams.

faq.question: Can MCP save the files for me?
faq.answer: The documented MCP tools return post details or download links. The CLI performs local saving and Bilibili stream merging.

faq.question: Will it overwrite my files?
faq.answer: The workflow uses separate folders and checks existing files against the source list. It does not treat a skipped file as a new download.

faq.question: What happens when a download fails?
faq.answer: The workflow keeps successful files and lists failed items with the reasons available. It does not invent saved paths.
